title: Why I Built My Portfolio as a Self-Editable CMS
excerpt: A short note on the engineering decisions behind this site — ISR caching, a Redis-backed CMS, and why the whole thing updates without a redeploy.
body:
Most student portfolios are static — to change a line, you edit code and redeploy.
I wanted mine to work like a real product: **edit content from an admin panel,
see it live instantly, no rebuild.**

## The setup

- Every section (Career, Projects, Bookshelf, …) reads its data from **Upstash
  Redis**, falling back to bundled JSON defaults.
- An `/admin` panel writes edits back to Redis.
- The homepage uses **Incremental Static Regeneration** — it's served from the
  CDN, and each save calls `revalidatePath("/")` so the cache busts immediately.

The result: visitors get a fast, cached page, and I get instant edits. That
cache-on-write, invalidate-on-change pattern is the same idea behind a lot of
distributed systems — which is exactly the space I want to work in.

## What's next

I'll use this space to write about networking and systems topics as I learn
them. If you're a recruiter or researcher reading this — the
[contact form](/#contact) is the fastest way to reach me.
